summary: The recorded base reproduced retained growth and stale oversized returns in EAGLE and DFlash. At the exact candidate commit, submitted and independent real-gfx950 GPU tests showed exact returned lengths across growth, shrink, zero-length, and empty-batch boundaries while preserving the semantic mask prefix and never retaining padding on self.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before real-GPU sequence on the recorded base: after 2->7->1 batch changes, EAGLE returned 462 elements for required 66 and DFlash returned 168 for required 24; both retained the oversized tensors. Zero-length and empty-batch calls also returned stale oversized masks.
Candidate regression at exact commit: 5 passed on GPU, covering growth/shrink for both implementations, retained identity, nontrivial prefix preservation, shrink view storage, and DFlash None.

Independent candidate adversarial sequence for EAGLE and DFlash over batch/sequence pairs (2,5), (7,5), (1,5), (4,0), and (0,0); asserted exact formula-derived lengths, retained three-element identity, prefix equality, and true-only padding.
All changed Python source and test files compiled successfully.
Candidate diff has no whitespace errors.

gpu_execution.evidence: One visible AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950 executed the candidate regression and independent cases with Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 / HIP 7.2.26015, including the real create_flashinfer_kv_indices_triton launch.

remaining_limitations: No EAGLE or DFlash model weights were provided, so full HTTP/model-serving and semantic-generation validation were not performed.
No long-duration serving allocator-fragmentation measurement was performed; focused tensor identity and retained-size checks directly cover the reported retention mechanism.
Validation used one gfx950 GPU, not a distributed or multi-node workload.
The candidate changes only Python and tests; no native source changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
NUMA balancing was enabled and produced an AIter warning, but the real GPU kernel tests completed successfully.
